## Project Overview

The goal of this project is to examine how racial and socioeconomic inequalities in school discipline and law enforcement contact vary across Charlotte Mecklenburg Schools (CMS). I'm also looking to explore how these patterns relate to the geographic distribution of schools in Mecklenburg County. I'm interested in how these findings connect to the historical contextualization surrounding school segregations and other inequalities. I will begin by examining the racial and economic breakdown of schools and then examine how suspension rates, law enforcement referrals, and school-related arrests interact with these demographic features. From a geographic lens, I plan to map these demographic differences and connect this to broader historical and institutional systems. While my initial research questions were hoping to consider neighborhood segregation, school boundaries, and juvenile/young-adult involvement in the criminal legal system, after reviewing the data I have access to these factors may be beyond the scope of this project. Ultimately, I hope to identify descriptive patterns specific to Mecklenburg County that reveal a relationship between school demographics, disciplinary practices, law enforcement contact, and geography, while also contacting these patterns to larger systems.
